title: Evidence and Sources
outcome: By the end, I can separate citation presence, link validity and support for an exact claim.
scenario: A fictional catalogue answer contains three factual statements and cites existing records.
given: Record R: book Ocean Maps has 80 pages and is available on shelf 2.
Claims: 80 pages [R]; shelf 2 [R]; suitable for every child [R]. All three citations resolve to R.

steps.label: Break into claims
steps.detail: Count three factual claims rather than treating the answer as one blob.

steps.label: Check links
steps.detail: All three citation links resolve to the intended R.

steps.label: Check exact source support
steps.detail: R supports page count and shelf, not universal suitability.

steps.label: Report separately
steps.detail: Citation presence 3/3; link validity 3/3; supported claims 2/3.

explanation: An existing citation is not automatically evidence for every nearby sentence. Read the cited passage and compare its exact scope with the claim. The universal suitability statement extends beyond what R says. Remove or qualify unsupported content; adding more copies of the same link does not create the missing evidence.

counterfactual.change: Change the third claim to “the record does not assess suitability”.
counterfactual.prediction: That statement accurately describes the supplied record’s limits.
counterfactual.reason: R gives pages and shelf only; it contains no suitability assessment.

student_task: Why is the original answer not fully supported despite having citations on every claim?
teacher_answer: One of the three claims is not entailed by its cited source; citation coverage and link validity do not measure claim support.
project_evidence: Attach source IDs to recommender explanation facts and separately audit whether each source supports its precise statement.
limits: Source support is relative to supplied records; those records can themselves be incomplete, outdated or incorrect.
review_note: New fictional case individually matched to this topic, with computations and policy traces checked. Use for supported practice; preserve the independent assessment.
